main_text.p: labant : scilicet quia solidi, & stabant sine inflexione. Ergo hamatæ istæ à Gallis, quarum alterum etiam genus, quod non anulis solis sed & squamis constat. Lorica squamea. Græci φολιδωτὸς vocant, vel λεπιδωτὸς, à squamis piscium vel serpentum. Sic Lucullum Plutarchus scribit, ipso die quo pugnauit in Tigranem, indutui habuisse In Lucul. ϑώρακα ἀ-ἀνδρὸς φολιδωτὸν : loricam ferream squameam. Et Dio Cassius, Macrinum Imperatorem abstulisse Prætorianis In Macr. καὶ[?] ϑώρακας καὶ[?] λεπιδωτὰς, loricas squameas : notesque ab his exemplis, honestiorum plane has fuisse. Eius textum & consertio. Has dico hamis & laminis solidis simul constitisse. ex Silio qui Flaminium Consulem armans:

p.i: Loricam induitur. tortos huic nexilis hamos
Ferro squama rudi, permissoque asperat auro.

main_text.p: Et Isidoro : Squama est lorica ex laminis æreis vel ferreis concatenata in modum squamarum piscis. Ipsas ergo squamas catenæ iungebant. Tertullianus illustratus, De Pall. cap. IIII. Tertullianus hanc intellegit & Alexandro Magno tribuit: Pectus squamarum signaculis discul ptum (malo discalptum) textu pellucido tegendo nu-dauit.

p.i: — rutilum thoraca indutus aënis Lib. xi. Horrebat squamis.

main_text.p: Silius: Horridus & squamis & equinâ Curio cristâ. Lib. viii. Hanc aut priorem idem:

p.i: At laterum textus spatiosaque pectora seruat Lib. iiii. Nexilis innumero chalybum subtemine thorax:

main_text.p: Hasipsas Squamas etiam Plumas video dici, à specie pa-ri. Plumæ quid? In Statio: —— ensem germani in corpore prefsit, Lib. xi. Qua male jam plumis imus tegit inguina venter.
Atque explicat ibi Luctatius, laminis. Parthorum assiduum hoc tegmen, etiam in equis. Parthorum cataphractæ. Iustinus: Munimen-

page.notes: Greek sign after "Prætorianis" and before "ϑώρακας" is an abbreviation mark (cŭ-like), read as καὶ with [?]; the first Greek word of the line break "ἀ-" / "ἀνδρὸς" and the initial letter of "ϑώρακα" are uncertain. "Luctatius" has a ct ligature, read as such. Catchword "tum" and signature "C" are at the foot. The last paragraph ends with the printed hyphen of "Munimen-" and the catchword "tum" is not repeated in the text.
